full_judgment:
Badrul Haider Chowdhury, J.- This appeal by special leave arises out of a judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Revision No. 539 of 1978 refusing quashment of the proceedings in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 687 of 1978 of the Court of the Sessions Judge, Bakerganj. 

 2. One Abdul Awal, respondent No. 2 allegedly sent a telegram to the Sessions Judge, Bakerganj making various allegations against Mr. Haripada Biswas, Magistrate, First Class, Jhalokati, the appellant, that he took signature on four sheets of blank white paper in his chamber purporting to show an amicable settlement of the dispute in M R. Case No. 40 of 1978 which was pending before his Court. The allegation is that the Magistrate obtained his signatures on blank sheet without his consent and concurrence. The Sessions Judge started on the footing of the telegram a suo motu Miscellaneous Case No. 687 of 1978 and called for the records of M. R. Case No. 40 of 1978 in exercise of jurisdiction under section 435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and stayed all further proceedings of the aforesaid M.R. Case and directed the appellant to submit a report to his Court regarding the allegations made in the said telegram. The appellant moved the High Court Division in criminal revision for quashing of the proceedings under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The learned Judges discharged the Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 687 of 1978 holding that section 435 Criminal Procedure Code has given ample powers to the Sessions Judge for conducting the impugned enquiry. The learned Judges observed: 

 "28.6.78. Perused the telegram just received. As appears from this telegram it has been sent by one Abdul Awal representing himself as complainant in M.R. case No. 40/78 pending in the Court of Mr. H P. Biswas, Magistrate, 1st class Jhalokati. There are in this telegram serious allegations of Judicial misconduct and high handedness against Mr. H. P. Biswas, Magistrate, 1st, class. 

 Let a criminal misc case be started on this Telegram and let a copy of this Telegram be forwarded to the learned Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Jhalokati, asking him to send the record of the above mentioned M. R. case along with a report of the Magistrate concerned to this Court direct forthwith through special messenger so that the same may reach this court by 6.7.78. Meanwhile the further proceedings of that M.R. Case are stayed until further order." 

 3. The High Court Division has relied on Section 435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. That section confers revisional powers so as to satisfy the Court as to the legality and regularity of any order passed therein. It would be noticed that the impugned order of the Sessions Judge is to the effect ''Let a criminal miscellaneous case be started on this telegram" and then he directed "Meanwhile the further proceeding of that M.R. case are stayed until further order." Here the learned Sessions Judge is taking cognizance of a case by issuing a suo motu Rule. How cognizance will be taken of an offence is provided by Section 190 of the Criminal Procedure Code and it provides by which Court such cognizance should be taken. Then section 193 provides in the following terms: 

 The provision is explicit and clear. In the instance case the Sessions Judge purported to take cognizance of an offence as a Court of original jurisdiction This is not permitted by law. The High Court Division has fallen into an error by relying on section 435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which provides concurrent revisional jurisdiction to the High Court, Sessions Judge, or District Magistrate which conferred power to call for records of inferior courts for examining any proceeding for the purpose of satisfying itself of himself as to the correctness, legality or propriety of any finding, sentence or order recorded or passed and as to legality of any proceeding of such inferior court and may when calling for such record direct that the execution of any sentence may be/suspended if the accused is in confinement, that he be released on bail or on his own bond pending the examination of the record." This power is given obviously when a proceeding is pending before the inferior court which is adjudicating issue between two contesting parties. But the Sessions Judge here has initiated a new proceeding against the Magistrate himself starting a criminal miscellaneous case. The proceeding is still pending before the Magistrate and the allegation is that he obtained some signatures on blank papers from the person who in the pending case is figuring as a party. The proceeding is still pending but allegedly he sent a telegram to the Sessions Judge complaining of the conduct of the learned Magistrate. This does not come within the purview of the revisional jurisdiction. There is some other provisions for such contingency. Should the Sessions Judge be of the opinion that the conduct of the Magistrate concerned required to be enquired into he could take resort to the superintending power of the Court and refer the matter to the High Court Division or to appropriate authority instead of starting a Miscellaneous case against the Magistrate for which no authority has been given by the Code. On the contrary it has been expressly prohibited by the Code. To allow the continuation of proceeding would amount to abuse of the process of Court and for securing ends of justice such proceeding is liable to be quashed. To hold to the contrary is to put the trial court in terrem thereby undermining the very structure of the administration of justice for which the Courts exist. But here the learned Sessions Judge has travelled beyond his jurisdiction by initiating a Miscellaneous Case himself which is not permissible in law. The proceeding must therefore, be quashed. 

 In the result, therefore this appeal is allowed, the decision of the High Court Division is set aside and the proceedings in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 687 of 1978 of the Court of Sessions Judge; Bakherganj are hereby quashed.
